102: For more information on recording late data in the ILR, refer to ’The impact of incomplete information’ in the ILR provider support manual.

Support funding

Learning support

103: You can access this funding through DWP funded adult skills fund and you record this against a learner’s learning aim in the ILR specification.

104: If you record learning support against a learning aim in the ILR, you will earn a fixed monthly rate of £150. We expect the total you earn from the monthly rate to be enough to cover your costs. If the cost of providing support to a learner exceeds the total earned from the fixed monthly rate, you can claim this excess through the EAS.

105: For learning aims with a planned length of less than one calendar month, our funding calculation will calculate the £150 appropriately in most cases, you should not need to use the EAS to claim the learning support. However, if you see that this funding has not been reflected in your funding reports, and we expect this to be in exceptional cases only, then claim the learning support through the EAS.

106: If learning support is more than £19,000, you can claim exceptional learning support above £19,000 using the cost form. You do not claim the amount above £19,000 through the earnings adjustment statement. The EAS can only be used for claiming the amount up to £19,000 (subtracting what you may have earned through the ILR). For more information, refer to the Adult skills fund: funding rules.

Learner support

107: Learner support is available to provide financial support for learners with a specific financial hardship preventing them from taking part or continuing in learning.

108: Learner support is not formula-funded so you cannot claim it through the ILR. How you claim learner support depends on the contract type the learner requiring support is funded under. If the learner support relates to learning delivered under a:

grant-funded contract, you must complete a mid-year funding forecast, a year-end and final funding claim to receive funding for learner support

procured ASF contract you must claim the support through the EAS

109: For further information, see the earnings adjustment statement and funding claims guidance.

Procured DWP funded ASF provision

110: If you have a contract with us from the most recent adult education budget (AEB) procurement (for delivery from August 2023) you must use the LDM code 388 (‘Adult Education Budget procurement 2023’) for all learning aims in this contract that started for delivery from 1 August 2023. This LDM code distinguishes between our procured and grant-funded contracts so we can identify which contract will pay for provision. Failure to record this code correctly may result in ILR errors or no payments.

111: Table 6 shows the LDMs you should use to indicate which contract you wish to use to pay for different types of adult delivery, and when they are valid.

Table 6: LDM codes for recording the contract

Type of Learning All learning aims

ASF non-procured No LDM

AEB procured learning, in the procurement which started delivery from August 2023 LDM 388

Non-procured provision within FCFJ

LDM 378

Procured provision within FCFJ, in the procurement which started delivery from August 2023 LDM 378 and 388

Funding reports

112: We will continue to provide funding reports to show you what funding we have calculated for you. These will range from headline funding reports to detailed reports at learner and learning aim level, like the funding summary reports and occupancy reports we provided last year. We will publish more detailed guidance in the funding reports guidance.

113: You will receive a set of reports when you submit your ILR data that will indicate how much you have earned. There will be 2 main reports for formula-funded adult skills fund provision that we fund:

occupancy report - this report gives the most detailed information at learner and learning aim level

funding summary report – this report gives you the aggregated information by month and for each funding line type (subcategories within the budget)

114: All learning aims that started before 1 August 2024 and continue into the year 2026 to 2027 should remain being recorded in the ILR using funding model 35 (‘adult skills’). We will continue to use the funding calculation from 2023 to 2024 for these learning aims. We will merge the information from the calculations for funding model 35 and funding model 38 into a single updated occupancy report, and similarly the funding summary report will contain information from both calculations. We will publish more detailed guidance in the funding reports guidance.

learners eligible for this offer are fully funded for their FCFJ learning aim

we increase the weighted rate by £600 for eligible aims in category code 45 (‘Free Courses for Jobs rate 1’) or by £150 for eligible aims in category code 46 (‘Free Courses for Jobs rate 2’)

72: You should use the learning delivery and monitoring (LDM) code 378 (Free courses for jobs offer) for all FCFJ aims for both 19 to 23 and 24+ learners. This will ensure you earn funding for the £150 or £600 uplifts.

73: All FCFJ learning aims with LDM code 378, irrespective of age, are funded through your FCFJ funding line.

74: You should only use LDM code 382 when recording learners continuing their learning from funding year 2023 to 2024 who met the low wage eligibility criteria. SAs can also set their own wage threshold (below which adults with an existing Level 3 can access FCFJ). You must not use LDM code 382 for any starts on or after 1 August 2024.

75: For starts on or after 1 August 2026 Mayoral Strategic Authorities can set their own rates and uplifts for FCFJ qualifications. Foundation Strategic Authorities [FSAs] have some limited flexibility to use their ASF FCFJ allocation to fund additional qualifications which are not part of the national offer. The FSAs are responsible for notifying you about any qualifications where this flexibility applies. For these qualifications however, the funding calculation will not increase the weighted rate by £150 or £600.

King’s Trust team programme

76: The programme rate is the same as last year at £3,204. This programme rate is the same for both employed and unemployed learners. We do not apply uplifts for disadvantage and area cost to the programme rate.

77: You will earn the funding rate for the award or certificate in ‘Employment, Teamwork and Community Skills’. The qualifications you can use are in table 3. You must also record the learners on the ILR using the LDM code 331.

Table 3: Qualifications for the programme 2026 to 2027

Qualification Title Learning Aim Reference

Certificate in Employment, Teamwork and Community Skills 60023995

Certificate in Employment, Teamwork and Community Skills (Entry 3) 60027629

Award in Employment, Teamwork and Community Skills 60032868

78: If the funding rate is lower than the programme rate, you can claim additional funding from the qualification rate up to the value of the programme rate. To claim this additional funding, you must use the Earnings adjustment statement adjustment type called ‘Kings Trust’. We will monitor the amounts being claimed.

79: Table 4 shows the qualification funding rates, the maximum programme rate and the maximum additional funding you can claim where appropriate. If the funding rate for the aim is uplifted for area cost and disadvantage you must adjust the additional claim accordingly using the maximum programme values in the table below. For example, a fully funded award when uplifted for area cost and disadvantage has a value of £665. The maximum additional funding is therefore £3,204 - £665 = £2,539.

Table 4: The rates for the programme for starts on or after 1 August 2026

Heavy goods vehicle (HGV) driver training

80: The level 2 learning aims that prepare learners for the HGV licence are Ofqual regulated qualifications. These are funded in the same way as other regulated learning aims and can be found on FALA with category code 50.

81: The HGV medical and certificates of professional competence (licence) have their own rates that allow eligible learners to be reimbursed for the cost. The HGV medical has category code 51. The certificates of professional competence (licence) have category code 52.

82: The HGV medical and certificates of professional competence do not attract disadvantage or area cost uplifts, and we do not hold back funding for achievement or completion.

Construction skills certification (CSCS) cards

83: The CSCS cards have their own rates that allow eligible learners to be reimbursed for the cost when delivered alongside specific qualifications. Refer to the Adult skills fund: funding rules for more details.

84: CSCS cards have category code 76. Refer to LARS category codes for more details.

85: CSCS cards do not attract disadvantage and area cost uplifts. We do not hold back funding for achievement or completion.

Our earnings method

Principles

86: The following principles apply to our approach to your earnings:

funding is distributed over the duration of the course starting from the date the learner started

you earn funding for what you deliver, when you deliver it

funding is directly linked to achievement or completion depending on your type of contract and when the learning aim started

for aims funded through a grant contract and started on or after 1 August 2024, funding is directly linked to the learner completing the learning aim or gaining employment

for aims funded through a grant contract and started prior to 1 August 2024, funding is directly linked to the learner achieving the learning aim or gaining employment

38: This ‘other funding adjustment’ factor increases or decreases the funding for that learning, including the achievement or completion funding. However, it does not change learning support funding.

39: If there is also a factor for prior learning recorded, we multiply the ‘funding adjustment for prior learning’ factor by the ‘other funding adjustment’ factor and apply it to the appropriate funding.

Our funding rates

Principles

40: The list of regulated qualifications approved for public funding are on find a learning aim that we update regularly. For information about what is eligible for public funding, refer to qualifications and public funding.

41: As rates can change between and during academic years (because of policy change or changes to the learning aim), we fund each learning aim at the rate that applies when the learner starts that learning aim. This principle is the same for a new start in the current funding year and a continuing learner from previous years. This rate will apply for the full duration of the learning aim and does not change between funding years.

42: The amount you earn recognises the relative value and costs of delivering provision in different sectors and subjects. We set the rates using the following criteria:

funded guided learning hours (GLH)

hourly rates that recognise the relative costs of delivering training in different sectors and subjects and provides a boost for training in those sectors identified as having greatest skills needs

Sector uplifts are based on the Sector Subject Area (SSA) that awarding organisations decide. The Register of Regulated Qualifications and the Access to Higher Education websites record the SSAs. Some components of qualifications can have multiple SSAs, where this happens, we set the SSA.

43: We have some exceptions that do not use the criteria above. In these instances, we set rates for some policy areas and specific learning aims such as:

work experience

HGV medical

HGV certificates of competence

CSCS cards

44: We add an uplift to the rate for all learners on FCFJ, more details can be found in paragraph 71.

45: We refer to rates as ‘unweighted’ when calculated using the base rate of £6.00 per hour. Once we have calculated the rate using the appropriate skills funding band, we refer to it as the ‘weighted rate’. After we apply the uplifts, we refer to the ‘aim value’, as noted in the ‘main occupancy report’. For more information on funding reports see the funding reports section.

46: All rates shown on find a learning aim are fully funded rates for learners aged 19 and above. We adjust these rates through the funding formula according to our policy (for example, if the government contributes only part of the full rate).

47: All learners funded through the 16 to 19 funding model that turned 19 in their second or subsequent funding year of a single programme of study are funded through the 16 to 19 funding model.

48: Our rates do not change depending on how you deliver the learning (for example, by delivering it on-line compared to in the classroom). Where rates are based on GLH, the rate is always the funded GLH in FALA regardless of how many hours you deliver the learning in.

Funding rates

49: We fund each GLH that is assigned to the qualification at an hourly rate, depending on the skills funding band assigned to the SSA of the qualification (see table 1). Each qualification is funded according to the specific GLH and SSA assigned to the qualification. Where a learning aim had a rate set in 2025 to 2026 (or earlier) and is continuing into 2026 to 2027, this rate remains unchanged for 2026 to 2027.

50: SAs are responsible for setting their own funding rates, where they do so these rates will form the basis of the funding calculation for provision funded by SAs and will be displayed in FALA.

51: Funding rates for individual qualifications are determined by multiplying the relevant hourly rate for the SSA of the qualification by the number of GLH as assigned by the awarding organisation and recorded on Ofqual’s register of regulated qualifications.

52: We use the GLH assigned by the awarding organisation and as recorded in Ofqual’s register. Where an awarding organisation amends the GLH for a qualification on Ofqual’s register, we may not automatically reflect this change in the associated funding rate. Therefore, there may be a difference between the GLH recorded on Ofqual’s register and the GLH we are using for the funding rate.

53: FALA shows the funded GLH in addition to the Ofqual GLH, so it is clear where there is a difference.

54: The Quality Assurance Agency for Higher Education (QAA) regulates Access to Higher Education Diplomas. The GLH for these qualifications is set at 600 hours.

Skills funding bands

55: Each SSA at tier 2 level is assigned to one of the 5 funding bands, see table 1. The funding bands for each SSA tier 2 are set out in annex 1.

56: We set all unweighted rates using the base rate of £6.00 per hour.

Table 1: adult skills funding rates by band

Adult skills funding band Base Low Medium High Specialist

Hourly adult skills funding rate £6.00 £7.20 £8.40 £9.60 £12.00

57: Here is an example of how we set rates taking Learning aim reference 60008817 Diploma in Engineering with funded GLH of 360:

The unweighted rate is calculated by multiplying the funded GLH of 360 by the base rate of £6.00 - this gives an unweighted funding rate of £2,160.

The weighted rate is calculated by multiplying the funded GLH of 360 by £9.60 (which is the hourly adult skills funding rate for high funding band that engineering SSA is in) - this gives a weighted funding rate of £3,456.
